ROOMS.title: The Volcano Lab
ROOMS.scenario: The monitoring lab on a restless volcano just lost power and the vault door slammed shut. The gas sensors are spiking. Every answer is part of the door code. Solve all 5 clues before the evacuation siren sounds.

clues.label: Clue 1
clues.q: The seismometers show swarms of small earthquakes that keep getting shallower. Molten rock is rising under the volcano. While it is still underground, what is that molten rock called?
clues.hint: Once it erupts onto the surface, it gets a different name: lava.
clues.exp: Magma is molten rock underground. Rising magma cracks rock as it moves, which causes swarms of small quakes.

clues.label: Clue 2
clues.q: The gas sample shows the magma is rich in silica, so it's thick and sticky. What property measures how much a liquid resists flowing?
clues.hint: Honey has more of it than water. Starts with V.
clues.exp: High-silica magma has high viscosity. It traps gas bubbles until the pressure blasts them out.

clues.label: Clue 3
clues.q: Use clue 2: thick, gas-rich magma, and a steep cone built from layers of ash and lava. What type of volcano is the lab sitting on?
clues.hint: Mount St. Helens is one. It has two names: one starts with C, the other with S.
clues.exp: Composite volcanoes (stratovolcanoes) erupt explosively because their sticky magma traps gas.

clues.label: Clue 4
clues.q: The warning screen says the deadliest danger here is a fast-moving avalanche of hot gas, ash, and rock racing down the slope. What is it called?
clues.hint: Two words. The first means 'fire-broken' in Greek. The second is what water does in a river.
clues.exp: Pyroclastic flows can move over 100 km/h and are hundreds of degrees hot. Nobody can outrun one, so evacuating early is the only defense.

clues.label: Clue 5
clues.q: Vault code: type the FIRST LETTER of each answer from clues 1 to 4, in order (4 letters).
clues.exp: Door open! Magma + high Viscosity = a Composite volcano that can send Pyroclastic flows. Evacuate to high ground away from valleys, which channel pyroclastic flows and lahars.

ROOMS.title: The Flood Zone
ROOMS.scenario: Spring snowmelt and heavy rain are pushing the river toward flood stage above a small Idaho town. Your team is locked in the county emergency center. Build the 5-part flood plan to open the door and warn the town.

clues.label: Clue 1
clues.q: Rain and snowmelt that can't soak into the frozen ground flow across the surface into streams. What is this water called?
clues.hint: It runs off the land. One word.
clues.exp: Frozen or paved ground can't soak up water, so more of it becomes runoff and rivers rise fast.

clues.label: Clue 2
clues.q: All the land that drains into this one river is its drainage basin. What is another name for a drainage basin?
clues.exp: A watershed collects every drop that falls inside its divides. The Snake River's watershed covers most of southern Idaho.

clues.label: Clue 3
clues.q: The flat, low land along the river that gets covered with water when the river overflows its banks. Great farmland, risky place for houses. What is it?
clues.hint: Flood + a flat, open area of land.
clues.exp: Floodplains are built from sediment the river drops during floods, which is why they're so fertile and so flood-prone.

clues.label: Clue 4
clues.q: In 1976, an earthen dam in eastern Idaho failed while it was being filled for the very first time, sending a wall of water toward Rexburg. What was the dam's name?
clues.hint: Same name as the jagged mountain range near Jackson Hole.
clues.exp: The Teton Dam failed on June 5, 1976. Its flood swept through towns along the river, including Rexburg.

clues.label: Clue 5
clues.q: Final lock: the National Weather Service says 6 inches of fast-moving water can knock an adult down, and 12 inches of rushing water can carry away most cars. Add 6 + 12 to the YEAR the dam in clue 4 failed. What is the code?
clues.exp: Door open! Code 1994. Never walk or drive into flood water. The National Weather Service slogan is 'Turn Around, Don't Drown.'

ROOMS.title: Quake City
ROOMS.scenario: A strong earthquake just shook Quake City and the seismology lab is on lockdown. To unlock the door, protect yourselves, read the seismograph, find the epicenter, and enter the keypad code.

clues.label: Clue 1
clues.q: The shaking starts! What 3-part action should everyone in the lab do right now? (Type all three actions.)
clues.hint: Get low, get under something sturdy, and hang on...
clues.exp: Drop, Cover, and Hold On. Get down before the shaking knocks you down, protect your head and neck, and hold on until it stops.

clues.label: Clue 2
clues.q: The seismograph caught two kinds of body waves. The fastest one arrives first and pushes and pulls the rock like a spring. What is it called?
clues.hint: It's named for being first, or primary. One letter + 'wave'.
clues.exp: P waves (primary waves) are the fastest seismic waves and travel through solids, liquids, and gases. S waves arrive second.

clues.label: Clue 3
clues.q: The S wave arrived 20 seconds after the P wave. The lab's rule of thumb: every 1 second of gap means the quake is about 8 km away. How many km away was the quake?
clues.hint: Multiply the gap in seconds by 8.
clues.exp: 20 s × 8 km/s = 160 km. The longer the gap between P and S waves, the farther away the earthquake.

clues.label: Clue 4
clues.q: Three stations each draw a circle showing their distance. The point on the map where all three circles cross is directly above where the quake started. What is that point called?
clues.hint: 'Epi' means 'above.' The point underground where the quake starts is the focus.
clues.exp: Using three stations is called triangulation. The circles cross at the epicenter, right above the focus.

clues.label: Clue 5
clues.q: Keypad: take your distance from clue 3 and add Idaho's biggest recorded earthquake magnitude, the 1983 Borah Peak quake (6.9), written without the decimal point (69). What is the code?
clues.exp: Door open! Code 229. Idaho's 1983 Borah Peak earthquake was magnitude 6.9, the largest in the state's recorded history.
